question.text: Let the slope of the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> for some <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>  </mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><munder><mi>lim</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></munder><mfenced><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to ______.

solution.text:
We know that,

The slope of line 45x+5y+3=0 will be -9

Now, given 27r1+9r22=-9

Now, solving

L=limx→3∫3x8t2dt3r2x2-r2x2-r1x3-3x

Applying Newton Leibnitz Theorem and L'Hospital Rule we get,

⇒L=limx→38x23r22-2r2x-3r1x2-3

⇒L=723r22-6r2-27r1-3

⇒L=72-9r22-27r1-3

Now, using 27r1+9r22=-9 we get,

⇒L=729-3=12
